title: A single hard-core uniqueness threshold on the square lattice
formal: Is there a finite λ_c>0 such that the hard-core model on Z² has a unique Gibbs measure for every 0<λ<λ_c and more than one Gibbs measure for every λ>λ_c?
definitions: The graph has vertices Z² and edges between points at Manhattan distance one. A configuration η∈{0,1}^{Z²} is admissible if no edge has both endpoints equal to one. For a finite Λ⊆Z² and an admissible exterior configuration τ, the finite-volume conditional law assigns to each compatible configuration ξ on Λ probability λ^{∑_{v∈Λ}ξ(v)}/Z_(Λ,τ), and zero to incompatible configurations. A Gibbs measure is a probability measure supported on admissible configurations whose conditional law on every finite Λ given the exterior is this law, almost surely. Uniqueness and multiplicity quantify over all such measures, not just translation-invariant ones. The selected target is a single separating threshold and makes no assertion at λ=λ_c. No numerical localization of λ_c is required.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated proposition or its negation for the specified model. A numerical estimate of a candidate transition point, or separated small-activity and large-activity theorems, does not establish the single-threshold statement.
context: The source gives rigorous coexistence at sufficiently large activity and describes the proposed single critical activity; the numerical estimate is conjectural.
why: The lattice transition organizes the behavior of independent-set sampling and spatial correlations.

import_provenance.original_statement: Establish and locate a sharp critical activity separating uniqueness from phase coexistence in the hard-core model on Z², where independent sets have weight proportional to λ raised to their size. Closing the gap between rigorous uniqueness and coexistence regimes would clarify the transition underlying Randall’s sampling and mixing-time results.
